company.name: Fredun Pharmaceuticals
company.summary: Fredun Pharmaceuticals makes medicines in a factory near Mumbai and sells most of them abroad, and is now adding pet-health, supplement and wellness brands.
company.description: A medicine such as a blood-pressure tablet must be made, packed, approved in each country that buys it, and sold to someone who will pay. Fredun does this for generic medicines (copies of medicines whose original patents have ended) in its own factory in Palghar, near Mumbai. Distributors and importers in many countries buy them, mostly in Africa, Southeast Asia, the former Soviet region and Latin America. Government agencies also buy medicines through public tenders. Over the past few years Fredun has added pet medicines, food supplements, skin-care products, support braces and a wellness range, which it presents as a wider healthcare business.
company.ownership: This profile covers Fredun Pharmaceuticals Limited, a Mumbai-based company listed on BSE. It makes medicines and health products in its own factory, and also runs newer consumer and pet-health brands. Several of those brands, such as Freossi, BeautyFred and DAULCÉL, are product names and not separate listed companies.
products: Products sold under another company’s name
Food-supplement brands such as Mamalait and Fredmax
Skin products with added active ingredients
company.money: Fredun earns money when a distributor, importer, government agency or other customer pays for the medicines and products it ships. Its main costs are the chemical ingredients, factory work, getting each product approved in each country, selling and advertising, and interest on loans. Newer consumer brands usually cost money to launch before they bring in much, so adding many at once can hold back profit.
watch: How much of sales still comes from medicines sold abroad?
The export medicine business is the established part; the new businesses are not yet proven.
Does profit keep pace as sales grow?
Sales can rise quickly without profit rising by as much.
How long does Fredun wait to be paid?
Overseas distributors and government agencies pay on different schedules and some in foreign currencies.
Will the new factory space be used?
A new facility adds costs such as depreciation and staff even if orders do not arrive.
Are the new brands earning their launch costs?
Pet, supplement, skin-care and wellness brands need advertising and stock before sales build.
risks: Regulators or buyers change the rules
A country can delay or refuse a registration, change its import rules or change what it will pay. Fredun sells in many such markets.
A failed quality check or a recall can stop sales and damage the relationship with distributors.
The cost of active ingredients and the exchange rate can change faster than Fredun can change its selling prices.
Distributors and agencies in other countries can delay payment or fail to pay, which ties up cash.
Too many new businesses at once
Launching pet, supplement, skin-care, device and wellness lines together stretches management and money, and some may not earn back their costs.
A small company with a short record on its new lines
The new lines are recent and their results are described mainly by the company itself.

update: August 2026: sales almost doubled but the profit margin hardly moved

Fredun’s 6 August 2026 results release says total income for April–June 2026 was almost twice that of a year earlier, and profit also nearly doubled, while the profit margin was almost unchanged. The extra profit therefore came from selling more, not from earning more on each sale. The figures are unaudited, meaning not yet fully checked by the auditors. The company also gave shareholders two bonus shares for every share held in July 2026. The full-year figures at the end of this page cover an earlier period.
company.question: If a company’s sales almost double, has its profit per rupee of sales improved?
company.answer: Not necessarily. If profit also nearly doubled, the margin (profit as a share of sales) stayed about the same. Compare profit growth with sales growth to see whether it is selling more or earning more on each sale.
